MRI LEFT KNEE

Clinical details: 31-year-old. Left anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (hamstring graft) in 2023. Recurrent anterior knee pain over the last three months. No giving way.

Technique: Multiplanar multisequence MRI of the left knee at 3T.

Comparison: Correlated with the recent radiographs.

Findings:
Menisci: Both menisci are intact. No displaced meniscal fragment.
Cruciate ligaments: The ACL graft is intact and appropriately orientated, with satisfactory femoral and tibial tunnel positions. No tunnel widening or cyclops lesion. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.
Collateral ligaments: The medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex are intact.
Extensor mechanism: The extensor mechanism is unremarkable. Patellofemoral alignment is normal.
Articular cartilage: Partial-thickness fissuring of the patellar cartilage at the median ridge and lateral facet. Femorotibial cartilage is preserved.
Bone marrow: No bone marrow oedema or fracture.
Joint and soft tissues: Small joint effusion. No Baker's cyst. The surrounding soft tissues are unremarkable.

Impression:
1. Intact ACL graft with satisfactory tunnel positions.
2. Partial-thickness patellar chondral fissuring, a likely contributor to the anterior knee pain.
